material_systems.name: Water-Based Grain Filler

deep_grain.notes: Oak, hickory — deep pores absorb more filler

moderate_grain.notes: Ash, walnut — shallower pores, less absorption

filler.notes: Water-based grain filler for painted wood. Apply as skim coat with squeegee (flats) or brush (profiles). Wipe excess off cross-grain. Low VOC, water cleanup. White color for paint-grade work. Coverage per coat varies by grain depth.

material_systems.notes: Single filler system for all grain fill work. Color is white (paint-grade). Material system is a recommendation — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Coverage per coat. Deep grain (oak, hickory): 60 SF/GAL. Moderate grain (ash, walnut): 75 SF/GAL. Profiled surfaces may consume more material due to increased surface area. Waste factor 1.12 (12%) for squeegee/brush application.
assumptions: Coverage varies by grain depth — deep grain absorbs more filler per coat
Profiled surfaces increase effective surface area
Waste factor 12% includes material lost in cross-grain wipe-off

coverage_profiles.notes: Second prime coat (seal coat) uses parent spec's primer. Standard primer coverage on smooth, grain-filled surface. Better coverage than first prime (surface is now smooth, non-porous).
assumptions: Uses same primer product as parent spec
Grain-filled surface is smooth — standard primer coverage applies

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Prep sand before fill, sand between fill coats (first sand cycle)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for prep sand and first interstage sand. 1 sheet per 20 SF. Orbital sander on flats, hand sand on profiles.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 280-grit
consumables.usage: Sand between fill coats (second and subsequent sand cycles at QT4+)
consumables.notes: 280 grit for second interstage sand at QT4+. 1 sheet per 25 SF. Finer grit for progressively smoother surface.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.usage: Sand between fill coats (third sand at QT5), sand second prime (all tiers)
consumables.notes: 320 grit for QT5 third interstage sand and for sanding second prime coat (all tiers). 1 sheet per 25 SF.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 400-grit
consumables.usage: Final sand before second prime (QT5 only)
consumables.notes: 400 grit for QT5 final sand. 1 sheet per 30 SF. Hand work only — no orbital at this grit. Produces glass-smooth surface.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: Tack cloth after every sanding step before next application. Critical for grain fill — dust in filler creates texture defects.

required_inputs.purpose: Total SF of all grain-fill-enabled substrates (pre-converted from native UOM)

compatibility_rules.description: Grain filler compatible with all parent spec primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based grain filler is compatible with all primer types. Second prime coat goes over filler — standard primer adhesion.

compatibility_rules.description: Grain fill only on primed surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: Surface must be primed before grain fill. Filler adheres to primed surface, not bare wood. Parent prime spec runs first.

compatibility_rules.description: Grain fill only for paint coating type
compatibility_rules.notes: Stain-grade grain fill is a different process. This spec is paint-only.

risk_notes.topic: Insufficient grain fill leaving visible texture through paint
risk_notes.risk: Under-filled grain pores show through paint finish as surface texture, especially at higher sheens
risk_notes.mitigation: Follow QT-driven coat count. Higher sheens require more fill coats (align with QT). Inspect with angled light between coats.

risk_notes.risk: Excessive filler left on surface (not wiped off cross-grain) creates raised film that sands through to raw wood
risk_notes.mitigation: Wipe excess off cross-grain immediately after application. Skim coat technique — fill pores, not build surface.

risk_notes.topic: Sanding through filler into bare wood
risk_notes.risk: Aggressive sanding between coats removes filler from grain pores, negating previous coat
risk_notes.mitigation: Light sanding pressure. Level the surface, don't remove material from pores. Orbital sander with fine grit on flats only.

risk_notes.risk: Some grain fillers may have adhesion issues with certain primer chemistries
risk_notes.mitigation: Use water-based grain filler (AquaCoat) which is compatible with all common primer systems. Test adhesion on sample if using unfamiliar product.

material_notes.single_system_architecture: ONE material system: water-based grain filler. No primer/finish systems — second prime coat uses parent spec's primer. Simplest material spec in the system.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Coverage varies more by grain depth than any other variable. Deep-grain oak may consume 50% more filler per coat than moderate-grain ash.
material_notes.waste_factor: 12% waste factor accounts for material lost in cross-grain wipe-off and squeegee technique. Higher waste on profiled surfaces.
material_notes.sandpaper_consumption: Sandpaper is the primary consumable cost. QT5 uses 4 different grits across 9 sanding passes (prep + 3 between + final + prime sand).

assumptions.value: 60 SF/GAL deep grain, 75 SF/GAL moderate grain per coat
assumptions.note: Coverage varies significantly by grain depth and application technique. AquaCoat published data suggests 15-20 SF/QT (60-80 SF/GAL) for deep grain.
Waste from cross-grain wipe-off and squeegee technique. May be higher on profiled surfaces.
